5. Energy and finite thermal states

The original duty allowance was 681 J DC per attempt. I replaced its actuation portion with an explicit screw-drive calculation:

Four M4×0.7 radial drives moving 10 mm.
One M6×1 source drive.
A 25 N/mm source spring compressed approximately 23.2 mm to reach 580 N.
Paid raising and lowering friction.
Positive retention and preload capture.
No recovered-electricity credit.

The thread/collar friction coefficients and 60% drive efficiency remain introduced values.

Search-force history	Purchased energy per attempt	Per accepted service at 90% acceptance	Campaign: 576 attempts / 500 acceptances
Force rises approximately linearly	740 J	854 J	884 J
Full preload throughout search	847 J	973 J	1,008 J

The twenty extra fault attempts are included in the campaign denominator calculation.

The full-force case misses the energy target. The force–travel history is therefore a load-bearing physical quantity to measure, not a convenient duty-cycle assumption.

At full preload, the introduced elastic inventory is approximately:

Central spring: 6.73 J.
Bank normal compliance: 0.34 J.
Radial compliance: 1.72 J.

Total: 8.78 J. Lowering dissipates it through the paid release path.

Heat is propagated through the campaign

The revised thermal calculation assigns screw friction to the head and the remaining purchased energy to the finite shared tool. It propagates all attempts, short holds and ten 24-hour holds without resetting temperature.

At 40°C ambient, calculated peak bulk head temperature is:

43.1°C for gradual-force search.
44.4°C for full-force search.

Actual contact flash temperatures and gradients remain unresolved. The contact stock and pads must therefore be qualified at their actual operating temperatures, not merely at ambient.

The robot is a much larger energy consumer: about 33.3 kJ per accepted service at an introduced 300 W and 100 seconds per attempt. It is separately reported and financially charged. This is not a 1 kJ total-robot-energy operation.

Direct shop-energy allowances are 12 kWh per first-build head and 0.5 kWh per repeat head. The latter is 3.6 kJ per service over 500 services. Upstream embodied material energy is unquantified, not zero. The current work does not close a complete lifecycle-energy claim.
